坦普雷小吉他為加那利群島傳統撥弦樂器，屬弦鳴樂器，Hornbostel–Sach: The timple canario is a traditional plucked instrument of the Canary Islands, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.321-5. Its making can be traced back to the nineteenth century. In the course of its development two ways of playing appeared, with five strings and with four: on La Palma and in the north of Tenerife some players leave out the first string, D, and play it as a four-string ukulele; supporters of the five-string version regard this as less traditional, while four-string players hold that it is the older manner of playing, before the fifth string was added in the late nineteenth or early twentieth century. The usual tuning is GCEAD. Notable players include Benito Cabrera and Germán López.
坦普雷小吉他琴身採用優質木材製作，通常選用雲杉或松木作為面板，提供良好的共鳴效果: The body of the timple canario is made of good timber, usually spruce or pine for the soundboard, which gives a good resonance. The neck and head are mostly mahogany or koa, which gives durability and stability. The strings are nylon in double courses, which strengthens volume and resonance. The bridge and nut are of bone or a substitute for ivory. Inside there are a soundhole and bracing that tune the resonance, producing a particular metallic timbre.
坦普雷小吉他音色明亮清脆，具有獨特的金屬質感。其高音域表現尤為突出，音質輕盈透徹: The timple canario sounds bright and crisp, with a particular metallic quality. Its treble is especially strong, light and transparent, over a warm resonant foundation. The instrument has five double courses, and the resonant body produces rich overtones, which give the sound depth and carrying power.

The timple canario is a traditional plucked instrument of the Canary Islands, a chordophone, Hornbostel–Sachs 321.321-5. It usually has five strings, with the usual tuning GCEAD; on La Palma and in the north of Tenerife many players leave out the first string, D, and play it as a four-string ukulele. Supporters of the five-string version regard this four-string practice as less traditional, but four-string players hold that it is the older manner of playing, from before the fifth string was added in the late nineteenth or early twentieth century. Its players can be called timplistas.
相比古典吉他的柔和厚重，坦普雷小吉他音色更加靈動活潑；與烏克麗麗相比，則擁有更強: Beside the soft fullness of the classical guitar the timple canario is livelier and more agile; beside the ukulele it has more brightness and carrying power. Its particular resonance lets notes ring on well while keeping a clear grain. This traditional instrument of the Canary Islands has its range in the middle and upper register, and suits fast phrases and ornaments, showing the typical style of Spanish folk music.
